expect_red: a drag on the flyout keeps room for THE DRAWING -- what the caller measured, not a pixel constant and not the drawing's scrollport

mutations.contract: However far it is dragged, the flyout leaves the page a strip to be adjacent TO -- bounded by the current viewport, not by a pixel constant.
mutations.note: Adjacency IS the deliverable ("the DAG must remain visible beside it"), and a px-only max cannot deliver it: at VA.FLYOUT_WIDTH.max on a 1280px window the panel would leave 80px of page. The mutation is the obvious simplification -- clamp to the window instead of to the window minus the reserve -- which reads as correct and covers the page. The reserve is measured against the room left BESIDE THE PREVIEW PANE, not against the viewport: reserving 420px of window handed the reader back 420px of PANE and covered the diagram completely (measured in Chrome at 1600px with the panel at 1100 -- #topopane at 300..1038, wholly underneath). See the lesson, section 2. Re-anchored 2026-09-16 after review: the clamp now takes a MEASURED `keep` (the drawing's own width) beside the room, so the arithmetic moved one line. The browser-tier claim it used to be mistaken for now has its own entry, `flyout-yield-short-of-the-drawing`.
